Current marker: INTERVIEW-115-059de052b28150d3-PATCH-967106d8973b.

Manual tracing finds no flaw under the string-input contract:
- `solve("")` → `0`: iteration yields nothing; the set is empty.
- `solve("😀")` → `1`: the surrogate pair yields one code point, producing one set entry.
- `solve("😀😀")` → `1`: both iterations yield the same code point; the second adds no entry.
- `solve("e\u0301")` → `2`: the letter and combining accent are distinct code points, even though they display together.

Final complete `src/core.mjs`:
```js
export function solve(s) {
  return new Set(s).size;
}
```

The invariant is that the set contains exactly the distinct code points encountered, never separate halves of a surrogate pair. Use the existing synchronous `solve(s)` export or service wrapper; no dependencies, API changes, or test edits are needed.
